method: 33 fetches. (1) The speaker listing https://websummit.com/speakers/ (and /page/2/, opened before its gating was noticed) shows 20 speakers a page, none Brazilian; its page data marks the list 'authRequired': true with 'authFreeItems': 20 (47 pages in all), so the rest of the speaker listing is treated as behind login and was not crawled; its country filter works only in the browser (?country=Brazil returns the same unfiltered 20). (2) The public schedule's own server-rendered search route https://websummit.com/schedule/search/<term>/page/N/ was read for: brazil (4 pages), brasil (4), brazilian (2), sao paulo (1), rio de janeiro (1), nubank (1 of 32; fuzzy matches, no Nubank), itau (1 of 2), ifood (1 of 4; fuzzy, no iFood), sebrae (1), apexbrasil (1). (3) Every Startup Showcase session, via the schedule's public track filter (3 pages, 20 sessions, 487 speakers). In all 45 distinct sessions were read. Each speaker's company was matched against the 236 Brazil-country startups of brazil-2 (Web Summit's featured-startups listing), exactly and by containment, then checked by hand (false matches like 'ESG Data Core' vs 'Data²' dropped). Two web searches found no press list of Brazilian speakers. The local data/events and desks/programme/agenda.json held only the Serpro, São Paulo and German-Brazilian items already known. Speaker cards on the schedule give name, job title and company only, never a country, so 'why_brazilian' is what the page or the startup listing says. A full pass over the schedule (about 52 pages of 7 a day, four days) was not possible in budget: Brazilian speakers whose session or company text names neither Brazil nor a Brazil-listed startup (for example a Brazilian executive at a global firm) can be missed.

not_reached.what_happened: Not fetched: the listing's page data says authRequired true with 20 free items, so beyond the first 20 it is a logged-in listing. Page 2 had been opened (20 speakers, none Brazilian) before this was seen.
The country filter is applied by scripts only; the server returns the same unfiltered first 20.
Not read in full: about 52 pages of 7 sessions per day, beyond the 40-fetch budget. Covered instead by the schedule search and the Startup Showcase filter.
Not read: page 1 showed only fuzzy matches unrelated to those companies; left for a later pass.
